Fathom

One event, followed down every layer of the machine, on one clock. A three-stage RV32I core, synthesised to gates, mapped to Sky130 cells, placed and routed.

Open Move through time Descend from a line …to the instruction …to the pipeline …to the gates …to the silicon plan Help Another program

Open

Fathom opens with every layer of the machine on one scrub bar: the program's source, the compiler's IR, the assembly, the register file, the pipeline, and — once loaded — the gates and the placed cells. The header names the machine: a three-stage RV32I core, synthesised to gates, mapped to Sky130 cells, placed and routed. It is a model of that core, not of the computer in front of you.

Move through time

Arrow keys step one cycle; shift steps ten; the scrub bar goes anywhere. Every layer moves together. Here at cycle 43 the first byte of “hi” is retiring: the source line that caused it, the instruction, the registers holding the byte and the UART address.

Descend from a line

Click a source line, or press ↓, to descend. The line becomes the focus, the layer below opens as context, and the instrument jumps to the first cycle that line ran.

…to the instruction

Down again: the assembly in focus, the IR above and the register file below as context. The trail in the footer records each stop so the way back is exact.

…to the pipeline

The pipeline: one column per cycle, one row per stage. Yellow is the instruction the descent follows; dim yellow is an instruction held in place — a taken branch or a load-use dependency — and red is a bubble with a named cause.

…to the gates

The bottom layers load on demand. The gate layer shows switching activity per cycle and, for the cycle in focus, which nets toggled.

…to the silicon plan

The cells: every placed standard cell on the real die, dark; the ones switching this cycle, lit. Placed and routed on Sky130 — timing and DRC as reported in the artifact, not tape-out clean.

Help

? opens the help; it says what the machine is and is not, lists every key and click target, and names the agent face for anything that wants to drive the instrument programmatically.

Another program

The library has four programs, each chosen to show one thing: a call frame writing to a memory-mapped port, data-dependent branches, load-use stalls on a pointer walk, and a call across two compile units. This is popcount at a branch flush.
